educational_level: B.A. First Year Tangkhul Major & Collegiate Readers
notes: Classic tragic novel and drama included in the Manipur University B.A. Tangkhul syllabus. Explores complex psychological themes of hubris, ancestral vows, and reconciliation.

front_matter.title_page: Shongza: The Tragic Chronicle of Destiny and Clan Honour (2007)
front_matter.preface: Shongza is a cornerstone text of Tangkhul higher education, combining the narrative breadth of a novel with the tense dialogue of classical Greek and Shakespearean tragedy. It probes the depths of 'ngashan' (customary honour) and demonstrates the tragic human cost of unforgiving generational vendettas.

chapters.title: The Oath of Vengeance (Kashungwui Tui-ngashik)
chapters.summary: An ancient ancestral grievance sparks an oath between rival mountain chieftains.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Shongzana awui avashimwui thàng khuilaga kaphung kashangli yangsaye. Kum kachung ngaphalashu, awui avawui kathi chi awui lungli meikatha thada kazeiye. Ana awui uningnaobingli hang: 'Shangwui phashan kashiman-khalang, mikumona katha eina ringkapamsara? I tui-ngashik saye, mashung-kasa raser-ra!' Kha awui ava-va kachamna hang: 'Shongza, vashitsang-kasa eina vashitsang kacham rara; ngashankahaimilu!'
chapters.english_translation: Shongza unsheathed his father's ancestral dagger and gazed across the mountain frontiers. Though years had passed, the memory of his father's untimely demise burned like unquenchable fire in his breast. He told his clan brothers: 'If our lineage honour is degraded, how can we walk with head held high? I swear a sacred oath, justice shall be executed!' Yet his wise mother cautioned him: 'O Shongza, vengeance begetteth only destruction; grant forgiveness!'
grammar_notes: Honorific clan speech: 'Shangwui phashan' (dignity of the patriline).
Hortative contrast: oath of revenge vs maternal plea for clemency.
exercises: Contrast Shongza's concept of justice with his mother's plea.
Identify the traditional weapon featured in the scene.

chapters.title: The Trial Before the Village Hangva (Hangvali Adjudication)
chapters.summary: The village elders convene at the sacred megalith circle to arbitrate between the feuding families.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Village Hangvawui elder-bingna lungphung kashang ngalemli pamkazipserie. Awungshina ceremonial tui-khak honsaye: 'Hao ngashanli mikumo kashikan khui mashuk-mana. Ithum tui-ngalung eina mashung-kasa sakakhui leisaye.' Shongzana awui tuitam chitheiye, kha rival chieftain-na restitution pay-sakhavai cattle kala woven Haora shawl offer saye. Hangvana tui khaklaga tui-ngalung treaty seal saye.
chapters.english_translation: The elders of the Hangva gathered beside the ancestral megalithic stone circle. The village chief pronounced the opening adjudication formula: 'Under customary law, no man may take the law into his own hands. We must establish reconciliation through righteous restitution.' Shongza presented his grievance, and the rival clan offered restitution of cattle and ceremonial Haora shawls. The council rendered its verdict, establishing a binding covenant of peace.

vocabulary.meaning: megalithic stone platform, village council arena

grammar_notes: Legal adjudication verb: 'tui khaklaga' (having severed/adjudicated the dispute).
Traditional restitution goods: cattle and woven textile regalia.
exercises: Explain the importance of the megalithic platform (lungphung) in Tangkhul jurisprudence.
How does the Hangva resolve clan disputes?

chapters.title: The Reconciled Dawn (Zingkhamathān Kathara)
chapters.summary: Shongza chooses reconciliation over bloodshed, breaking the cycle of vendettas for future generations.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: Shongzana awui thàng sheath-li sheitsangserie. Ana theitserie: Mashung-kasana kashamli maphuma-mana, kha ringkapha kaphāli phumye. Khor ceremonial pot eina athum khani clan-bingna ngayei tui honserie. Ukhrul kaphungli zingkhamathān shoklakha, village yaronaobingna mathat-eina Hao Pheichak pheitserie. Shongzana hang: 'Ithuwui naorap thot pupup ngacham eina ringkapamsara!'
chapters.english_translation: Shongza sheathed his dagger into its scabbard. He realized: True strength lies not in shedding blood, but in preserving life and future generations. Drinking from the ceremonial rice-beer horn, the two clans sealed their sacred alliance. As dawn broke over the peaks of Ukhrul, the youth joined in the festive circle dance. Shongza proclaimed: 'Our children and grandchildren shall abide in enduring peace!'
grammar_notes: Climactic resolution: sheathing the weapon symbolizes transition from warrior vendetta to civic peace.
exercises: Discuss Shongza's internal character growth across the three chapters.

Chapter 3: Shongzana awui thàng sheath-li sheitsangserie. Ana
theitserie: Mashung-kasana kashamli maphuma-mana, kha ringkapha kaphāli
phumye. Khor ceremonial pot eina athum khani clan-bingna ngayei tui
honserie. Ukhrul kaphungli zingkhamathān shoklakha, village
yaronaobingna mathat-eina Hao Pheichak pheitserie. Shongzana hang:

Shongza sheathed his dagger into its scabbard. He realized: True
strength lies not in shedding blood, but in preserving life and future
generations. Drinking from the ceremonial rice-beer horn, the two clans

the youth joined in the festive circle dance. Shongza proclaimed: 'Our
children and grandchildren shall abide in enduring peace!'
